mentions.quote: A Brahmana may confidently take property from a Shudra
mentions.role: agent with legal right to appropriate Shudra property

entities.description: The priestly varna (social class) empowered by Manu to take property from Shudras, reflecting the dharmic hierarchy.
entities.justification: Explicitly named in 8.417 as the class entitled to seize Shudra property.

mentions.quote: A Brahmana may confidently take property from a Shudra; for he has nothing of his own, for his property may be taken by his master
he should diligently make the Vaishya and the Shudra perform their own duties
mentions.role: social group required to perform varna-specific duties under royal enforcement

entities.description: The lowest of the four varnas, defined in this passage as propertyless and duty-bound under royal coercion.
entities.justification: Named twice in 8.417 and 8.418 as a group stripped of property rights and subject to enforced duty-performance.

mentions.quote: he should diligently make the Vaishya and the Shudra perform their own duties; for those two, having fallen from their duties, would throw this world into confusion
mentions.role: social group whose duty-observance is enforced by the king

entities.description: The mercantile/agricultural varna whose adherence to duty is treated as necessary for cosmic-social order.
entities.justification: Explicitly paired with Shudra in 8.418 as a class the king must compel to observe dharma.

mentions.quote: He should diligently make the Vaishya and the Shudra perform their own duties
Day by day he should inspect the workshops and the vehicles, and the fixed income and expenditure, the mines, and the treasury
Thus a king, by settling all these legal proceedings, having cast off all sin, attains the supreme state
mentions.role: juridical authority whose proper conduct leads to liberation

entities.description: The ideal monarch whose diligent administration of justice, economic oversight, and varna enforcement is the subject of the concluding verses of Chapter 8.
entities.justification: Named or indicated in 8.418-8.420 as the central agent responsible for social order, economic management, and moral attainment.

mentions.quote: he should inspect the workshops and the vehicles, and the fixed income and expenditure, the mines, and the treasury
mentions.role: royal fiscal resource subject to daily inspection

entities.description: The royal storehouse of wealth, listed among the economic assets a king must personally monitor each day.
entities.justification: Explicitly named in 8.419 as part of the king's daily administrative duties.

mentions.quote: he should inspect the workshops and the vehicles, and the fixed income and expenditure, the mines, and the treasury
mentions.role: state economic resource under royal oversight

entities.description: Extractive mineral sites listed among the royal economic infrastructure requiring daily royal inspection.
entities.justification: Named in 8.419 alongside workshops and treasury as royal assets the king must regularly oversee.

mentions.quote: A wife, a son, and a slave—these three are remembered as having no property; whatever they acquire, that property belongs to him to whom they belong
for he has nothing of his own, for his property may be taken by his master

themes.justification: 8.416-8.417 explicitly establish that wife, son, slave, and Shudra hold no independent property—everything they earn reverts to the paterfamilias or master.

mentions.quote: He should diligently make the Vaishya and the Shudra perform their own duties; for those two, having fallen from their duties, would throw this world into confusion

themes.justification: 8.418 frames royal coercion of lower varnas to observe svadharma as a cosmic-political necessity to prevent world-disorder.

mentions.quote: Day by day he should inspect the workshops and the vehicles, and the fixed income and expenditure, the mines, and the treasury

themes.justification: 8.419 prescribes a detailed daily audit of economic infrastructure—workshops, vehicles, revenue, mines, treasury—as part of ideal kingship.

themes.topic: Judicial conduct as path to liberation

mentions.quote: Thus a king, by settling all these legal proceedings, having cast off all sin, attains the supreme state

themes.justification: 8.420 implicitly links dharmic jurisprudence to soteriological outcome: proper legal administration purifies the king of sin and leads to the supreme state (moksha or svarga).

themes.topic: Hierarchical social order and its cosmic stakes

mentions.quote: for those two, having fallen from their duties, would throw this world into confusion
whatever they acquire, that property belongs to him to whom they belong

themes.justification: The window as a whole implicitly treats the four-varna hierarchy and the patriarchal household as cosmic structures whose disruption threatens universal order (8.416-8.418).
